Actions in Cartesian space, at control frequency
Long‑horizon composition and recovery from failure
The 2022 recipe — keep the LLM in a box, let it emit text, and bolt on separate low‑level controllers — leaves the most capable models blind to geometry. The 2023 bet: put perception, and then action, inside the model itself.

01 · CONTEXT
Three papers, three entry points
PAPER 01 · MAR 2023
PaLM-E
Google · 562B parameters
An embodied multimodal language model: sensor data is injected into a pretrained LLM as tokens, and the model emits plans as text.
Contribution type
a model & a training recipe
PAPER 02 · JUL 2023
RT-2
Google DeepMind · up to 55B
A vision‑language‑action model: robot actions are written as text tokens, so one network both answers questions and drives the arm.
Contribution type
a general recipe (VLA)
PAPER 03 · MAY 2023
Voyager
NVIDIA · Caltech · UT Austin · Stanford
An open‑ended embodied agent: GPT‑4 writes code, verifies it, and stores working skills in a growing library — no fine‑tuning.
Contribution type
an agent architecture
Read together, they trace a single arc: generic knowledge → grounded perception → grounded action → grounded self‑improvement.

02 · PALM-E Perception as a sentence PaLM-E keeps the language model and changes the input. Images, robot states, and 3D scene representations are encoded into vectors with the same dimension as word embeddings, then interleaved with text to form a “multimodal sentence”. 01 A frozen‑or‑fine‑tuned PaLM decoder does the reasoning — 8B, 62B, or 540B. 02 An encoder maps one observation to q vectors; tokens land dynamically wherever the text puts them. 03 The output is still text — an answer, or a plan that sequences low‑level skills. INPUT SEQUENCE Given Q: How to grasp the blue block? A: MODEL OUTPUT “First grasp yellow block and place it on the table, then grasp the blue block.” modality token text token Key architectural claim: a 22B ViT plus a 540B LLM gives PaLM-E‑562B — at the time, the largest vision‑language model reported.
